node_definition.done_when:
Read the plan section with read_plan(view='section', section='s3') before starting; it is the authority. Measure first, before writing the refusal. In a scratch copy, make the followup append path in reckon/_store.py refuse whenever classify_followup says hides-work. Then run every test file under tests/ that appends a followup, found by a text search for the followups append op, append_to_list, followup_ops_from_manifest, and the HTTP plan patch with a followups key. Record the failing ids and the callers that would be refused, in a log in the run directory and in the manifest. That count is the scope of this node. Then land the refusal for both write paths, edit_plan's state ops and the HTTP patch path, through one function both call, built on classify_followup. Resolving, superseding and reading a followup are never refused. A caller that appends work as a followup is repaired, inside your fence if it lies in reckon/_store.py or reckon/followup_pointers.py. Otherwise it is named in follow_ons with the failing ids, never silenced. A test fixture is changed only where it encodes appending work as a followup, and each such change is named in the manifest. In a new tests/test_a_followup_that_hides_work_is_refused.py, built on plans written into a temporary docs directory, cover the section's five append cases plus resolving an existing followup that hides work. Execute the named negative control and confirm the no-section case is then written. The gate is the new test plus the files the measurement found. Run it at base and at head and list the files in the manifest. An evidence fragment at docs/evidence/fragments/work-is-a-section-not-a-followup/a-followup-that-hides-work-is-refused.html records the change and the measured population.
Run `date -u` first and treat that instant as your start; your deadline is 60 minutes later. Write your manifest before starting any long command. Run both gate arms with pytest-xdist (-n 8 --timeout=300), never serially. Start the base arm, from a `git archive` extraction of your base under /tmp in a directory named for this run, in the background, then run the head arm in the foreground, so they overlap. Each arm uses its own basetemp outside any repository and writes to its own new log path, which it never overwrites. Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder. Each log names its revision on the first line and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. The head arm adds no failure id; any added id means status blocked, naming each id. ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed Python paths report no finding the base did not. Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.
